clue.text: Obtained back anaesthetic at the same time

indicators.note: back tells us the word for obtained is to be read from right to left

parts.note: obtained means got
ether is an old general anaesthetic

explanation.surface: Someone receives an anaesthetic at the same moment as something else happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns only the word for obtained; the anaesthetic follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things jointly means doing them simultaneously, in one another's company.

clue.text: Cake expert races round

indicators.note: round says the word for races goes around the word for expert

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: A skilled baker hurries around making a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT races are motorcycle races held on the Isle of Man; 'round' wraps them around the expert word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a flat block, as in a cake of soap; in Scotland it is also a fudge-like sweet.

clue.text: Good passage on an old vessel

parts.note: an alley is a narrow passage between buildings

explanation.surface: A pleasant voyage aboard an ancient ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley was an ancient ship rowed by oars, often by slaves.

clue.text: Taught first officer wrong alarm signal

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word taught

parts.note: OC is short for Officer Commanding
a sin is a wrong or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: An instructor trained the first officer wrongly in alarm procedures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' sits after 'Taught', so it takes T; 'first officer' looks like a ship's mate, but OC (Officer Commanding) follows on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is a warning bell rung to raise an alarm.

clue.text: Urged to dump grit in tip

indicators.note: in says the word for grit is placed within the word for tip

parts.note: a tip or extremity is an end
grit means courage or determination

explanation.surface: An instruction to dispose of grit at the rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a rubbish dump, matching 'dump', but it means an extremity; 'in' places grit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be encouraged is to be urged on or spurred to act.

clue.text: A50 route to the south used every time

parts.note: A is taken as written and 50 is L in Roman numerals
a route is a way

explanation.surface: The A50 road heading south is the route taken on every journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The A50 is a British trunk road, but here A stays as A and 50 is the Roman numeral L; 'to the south' puts S at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on every occasion is doing it invariably.

clue.text: Quiet holiday in Cornish resort — a means of escape

indicators.note: in says quiet and holiday go inside the resort's name

parts.note: Looe is a fishing town and resort in Cornwall
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
hol is a short form of holiday

explanation.surface: A peaceful break in a Cornish seaside town as a way to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: Looe is a small resort in Cornwall, in south-west England; 'in' places quiet and holiday inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is a gap in a rule that lets someone evade it, an escape route.

clue.text: Vera is turning against hatred

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of vera and is are twisted into a new order

parts.note: on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: Vera is turning against someone out of hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges the six letters of Vera is, and the word for against follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike or loathing.

clue.text: Same dresses; not so many without a join

indicators.note: dresses means arranges, so the letters of same are put in order afresh

parts.note: less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Identical outfits with fewer seams in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dresses' rearranges SAME into SEAM, followed by LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no visible joins or stitching is smooth and continuous.

clue.text: Col. Black replaced device in cistern

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of the name are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: Colonel Black replaced a toilet-tank part, like a murder-mystery suspect turned plumber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges COLBLACK; Colonel Black evokes the board game of suspects but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballcock is a floating valve that controls the water level in a toilet tank.

clue.text: Wine shop takes elderly old boy back

indicators.note: back tells us both pieces are read together from right to left

parts.note: elderly means aged
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A wine merchant accepts an elderly former pupil back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses AGED followed by OB, giving BO then DEGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or wine bar.

clue.text: Use different case for "worth being honourably retired"

indicators.note: case for means the scrambled letters act as a holder around the word for worth
different says the letters of use are made into another order

parts.note: merit means worth or value

explanation.surface: A grammar note about putting a word in another case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns USE into E...US, which forms a 'case for' MERIT; the surface talks of grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor emeritus keeps the title as an honour after leaving the post.

clue.text: Cheat companion with terrible lies

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters of lies are mangled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A friend who tells dreadful lies is a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is Companion of Honour, a British award; 'terrible' rearranges LIES to ISEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To chisel someone is slang for to swindle or defraud them.

clue.text: Hormone relating to the kidneys found in a lunch?

indicators.note: found in says the kidney word is placed inside the lunch word

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal such as lunch
renal means relating to the kidneys

explanation.surface: A hormone made near the kidneys turns up in a midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'lunch' is a verb, to eat a meal; 'found in' puts the kidney word inside it after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenaline is the hormone of the adrenal glands, released in stress.

clue.text: Moving inland does find unwanted plants

indicators.note: moving shows the letters of inland does are shifted about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Female deer heading inland find weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges INLANDDOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandelions are common yellow-flowered weeds in lawns.

clue.text: Hoses are damaged by fish

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters of hoses are are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: Garden hoses are ruined by fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges HOSESARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A seahorse is a small upright marine fish with a horse-like head.

clue.text: Being in concert is getting older soldiers in

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the word for getting older

parts.note: ageing means getting older
RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

explanation.surface: Being at a concert, ageing troops are brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a British army corps; 'in' places them inside the word for getting older.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in concert is to act in harmony or accord with others.

clue.text: Finding incense in bottom of jug is annoying

parts.note: to incense is to anger

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Discovering incense at the bottom of a jug is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' looks like the fragrant stuff but is the verb, ANGER; 'bottom of jug' gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: Making someone cross is irritating them.

clue.text: Car driver takes first exit left as arranged

parts.note: the engine is what drives a car

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of exit

parts.note: red describes the political left

explanation.surface: A motorist takes the first exit on the left as planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car driver' looks like a motorist but is the ENGINE; 'first exit' gives E and 'left' is RED in politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Something engineered was contrived or brought about by planning.

clue.text: Put on assorted gates and front doors

indicators.note: assorted means the letters of gates come in a mixed order
front picks the opening letter of doors

explanation.surface: Fitting various gates and front doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assorted' turns GATES into STAGE; 'front doors' gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is staged when it is put on as a production.

clue.text: What it costs to hear a singer?

indicators.note: to hear says the word for a singer is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer

explanation.surface: How much is a ticket to listen to a vocalist?
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note, here the price.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-pound note is a price paid, the amount something costs.

clue.text: Display counter is to come down

parts.note: to land is to come down to the ground

explanation.surface: A shop display stand is to be taken down.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a free-standing unit, as in a kitchen or a store's display stand.

clue.text: Listed the fish he had brought round

indicators.note: brought round says the contracted he had goes around the fish

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he had
an eel is a snakelike fish

explanation.surface: A man lists the fish he caught and brought home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listed' looks like 'put on a list' but means a ship leaning over; 'brought round' wraps he'd around the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has heeled has tilted over to one side.

clue.text: Quickly head for somewhere safe?

parts.note: fast means quickly
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Advice to run quickly for safety.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastness is a stronghold or secure retreat.

clue.text: Cake ingredient is taken into the shower

indicators.note: taken into says is goes inside the shower word

parts.note: a shower of rain

explanation.surface: A baking ingredient is taken into the bathroom shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' looks like the bathroom fixture but is weather; 'taken into' places is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried grapes are a common fruit-cake ingredient.

clue.text: Tobacco never used by heartless Ida

parts.note: virgin means untouched or never used

indicators.note: heartless removes the centre, leaving the first and last letters of Ida

explanation.surface: Ida, a cold woman, never touches tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless Ida' loses its middle D to leave IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is a type of tobacco named after the US state where it is grown.

clue.text: Some find Boateng a gentleman of promise

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Fans find footballer Boateng a gentleman with real potential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks letters running across BoatENG A GEntleman.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage is to pledge or bind oneself, as in becoming engaged to marry.

clue.text: Offered to get Nurse Elizabeth a man!

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A nurse called Elizabeth lands herself a man.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the cipher of Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender something is to present or offer it formally, as in a resignation.
